slides.title: Understanding Recursive Functions
slides.prompt: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself. A recursive function requires a base case to terminate execution and avoid reaching the maximum recursion limit.
slides.codeSnippet:
def factorial(n):
    if n <= 1:  # Base case
        return 1
    return n * factorial(n - 1)  # Recursive case

slides.title: Tail Call Optimization in Python
slides.prompt: Does standard Python (CPython) perform automatic Tail Call Optimization (TCO)?
options: No, CPython does not optimize tail calls to preserve full call stack tracebacks
Yes, it optimizes all recursive calls automatically
Yes, but only if configured with sys.setrecursionlimit
slides.correctAnswer: No, CPython does not optimize tail calls to preserve full call stack tracebacks

slides.title: Recursion vs Iteration
slides.prompt: Why might an iterative approach (using loops) be preferred over recursion in standard Python?
options: To avoid function call overhead and stack depth limits (RecursionError)
Because Python loops cannot be interrupted
Because recursion only works with numeric values
Iterative loops run in multi-threaded hardware mode automatically
slides.correctAnswer: To avoid function call overhead and stack depth limits (RecursionError)
